finding.claim: deleteAccount performs no authorization: it calls canDelete() but discards the boolean result, so any caller can delete any account by id.
finding.source: Caller-supplied `id` and `User u` passed to deleteAccount (DELETE /accounts/{id} per comment on line 19). Precondition: attacker can invoke this method with any id while holding any valid user object.
finding.sink: accounts.remove(id) at src/AccountService.java:23 (destruction of another user's account).

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) entry point; u and id are caller-supplied
a = accounts.get(id) loads any account with no ownership filter
canDelete(u, a) evaluated but return value ignored; no throw, no if

finding.guards_checked: canDelete() (lines 9-11) is correct in isolation (admin or owner) but its result never gates the operation. assertCanDelete() (lines 13-17) is not called on this path. No other check between lines 20 and 23. closeAccount (lines 27-31) uses assertCanDelete and is not affected. Auth of `u` and origin of `id` could not be verified: the repo contains no HTTP/auth layer.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. canDelete() at src/AccountService.java:9-11 returns a bool, but line 22 calls it as a bare statement and discards the result. assertCanDelete() at lines 13-17 (which throws) is not called on the deleteAccount path (lines 20-24). No other check sits between line 21 and line 23.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: deleteAccount (src/AccountService.java:20-23) loads any account by id, discards the canDelete result at line 22, and removes the account at line 23, while the throwing guard assertCanDelete (line 29) is used only in closeAccount. Any caller holding a valid User can delete any existing account. The caveat is that the repo has no HTTP/auth layer, so whether an unauthenticated or low-privilege user can reach this method cannot be verified here; the missing check itself is real.
